scenario.name: Mandiant & Snowflake Joint Report (UNC5537), CISA & MITRE T1530 — Snowflake Single-Factor Session & QUERY_HISTORY Egress Forensics
scenario.overview: Imagine a massive cloud archive warehouse where a contractor’s stolen single-key password still unlocks the front door because neither a second approval buzzer nor an approved-visitor street list was turned on. Walking straight inside from an unfamiliar address, the intruder prints out the master floor map of every filing aisle, packs millions of customer records into compressed shipping crates in a private staging bay, and wheels the crates right out the loading dock. In this scenario (T1078.004, Mandiant & Snowflake Joint Report , UNC5537, CISA & MITRE T1530, Snowflake Single-Factor Session & QUERY_HISTORY Egress Forensics), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: single-Factor Password Authentication, then schema Discovery, then bulk Table Staging via COPY INTO @~. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Single-Factor Password Authentication, then Schema Discovery, then Bulk Table Staging via COPY INTO @~, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection pivots on CloudTrail Event 1001 correlated across the documented kill chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: Single-Factor Password Authentication in ACCOUNT_USAGE.LOGIN_HISTORY
stages.subtitle: Initial Access (T1078.004 - Valid Accounts: Cloud Accounts)
stages.description: Using an old key copied months earlier from a contractor’s compromised workstation, an outsider walks up to the archive warehouse from an unknown street address and unlocks the front gate with a single password because no second verification chime or neighborhood gate list stops them. Using historical credentials harvested from an infostealer infection on a contractor workstation, an external client authenticates to a Snowflake tenant account that lacks a Network Policy IP allowlist and has not enforced multi-factor authentication (SECOND_AUTHENTICATION_FACTOR = NULL in LOGIN_HISTORY) (logged in CloudTrail Event 1001 with AuditView=SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.LOGIN_HISTORY & SESSIONS, AuthenticationFactors=FIRST_AUTHENTICATION_FACTOR=PASSWORD, SECOND_AUTHENTICATION_FACTOR=NULL, ClientApplication=DBeaver_DBeaverUltimate / JDBC_DRIVER 3.14.4 from 198.51.100.214 so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes SELECT EVENT_TIMESTAMP, USER_NAME, CLIENT_IP, REPORTED_CLIENT_TYPE, FIRST_AUTHENTICATION_FACTOR, SECOND_AUTHENTICATION_FACTOR FROM SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.LOGIN_HISTORY WHERE IS_SUCCESS = 'YES' AND SECOND_AUTHENTICATION_FACTOR IS NULL; (which executes a structured SQL query or database administration command , SELECT EVENT_TIMESTAMP, USER_NAME, CLIENT_IP, REPORTED_CLIENT_TYPE, FIRST_AUTH so that pivots from database query access or SQL injection to direct operating system command execution or authentication bypass , T1078.004 during "Single-Factor Password Authentication in ACCOUNT_USAGE.LOGIN_HISTORY" under the database daemon's service account). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ LOGIN_HISTORY user=SVC_BI_ANALYTICS first_factor=PASSWORD second_factor=NULL client=JDBC_DRIVER / ⇠#1 ACK 1001) from Node ① (#1 External SQL Client (DBeaver)) to Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Customer PII Tables & Internal Stage).

keySpecs.value: SELECT EVENT_TIMESTAMP, USER_NAME, CLIENT_IP, REPORTED_CLIENT_TYPE, FIRST_AUTHENTICATION_FACTOR, SECOND_AUTHENTICATION_FACTOR FROM SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.LOGIN_HISTORY WHERE IS_SUCCESS = 'YES' AND SECOND_AUTHENTICATION_FACTOR IS NULL;

Enforce Snowflake Authentication Policies requiring MFA or OAuth/SAML SSO for all human users, mandate RSA key-pair or OAuth Workload Identity for service accounts (TYPE = SERVICE), and attach account-level and user-level Network Policies.
Initial Access (T1078.004 - Valid Accounts: Cloud Accounts)

stages.title: Stage 2: Schema Discovery & Privilege Enumeration in ACCOUNT_USAGE.QUERY_HISTORY
stages.subtitle: Discovery (T1087.004 - Account Discovery: Cloud Account)
stages.description: Inside the archive warehouse, the intruder runs an automated clipboard sweep across every hall, listing which master roles their key holds, which vaults exist on each floor, and which filing cabinets contain the highest-value customer ledgers. Once authenticated, the session executes automated discovery queries (SHOW GRANTS TO USER, SHOW DATABASES, SHOW SCHEMAS, and SELECT * FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES) recorded in SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.QUERY_HISTORY with SESSION_ID linkage (logged in CloudTrail Event 1002 with ActiveRole=ACCOUNTADMIN , Over-Privileged Legacy Service Account, DiscoveryQueries=SHOW GRANTS TO USER; SHOW TERSE DATABASES; INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES, SessionId=884120994102 so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes SELECT QUERY_ID, USER_NAME, ROLE_NAME, QUERY_TYPE, QUERY_TEXT, ROWS_PRODUCED FROM SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.QUERY_HISTORY WHERE SESSION_ID = 884120994102 ORDER BY START_TIME; (which executes a structured SQL query or database administration command , SELECT QUERY_ID, USER_NAME, ROLE_NAME, QUERY_TYPE, QUERY_TEXT, ROWS_PRODUCED F so that pivots from database query access or SQL injection to direct operating system command execution or authentication bypass , T1087.004 during "Schema Discovery & Privilege Enumeration in ACCOUNT_USAGE.QUERY_HISTORY" under the database daemon's service account). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ SHOW GRANTS TO USER SVC_BI_ANALYTICS; SELECT TABLE_CATALOG, TABLE_SCHEMA, TABLE_NAME, ROW_COUNT, BYTES FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES; / ⇠#2 ACK 1002) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 Snowflake Network Policy Gate), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Customer PII Tables & Internal Stage).

Stream SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.QUERY_HISTORY and SESSIONS into the enterprise SIEM and alert on non-scheduled SHOW GRANTS / INFORMATION_SCHEMA enumeration from interactive SQL clients (DBeaver, Rapeflake, SnowSQL).

stages.title: Stage 3: Bulk Table Staging via COPY INTO @~ & GET File Egress Forensics
stages.subtitle: Exfiltration (T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage)
stages.description: Instead of carrying folders out one by one, the intruder dumps entire customer aisles into compressed bundles inside their personal staging closet and hauls the packed bundles straight out the exit ramp, leaving giant weight spikes on the warehouse shipping scale. To compress and export high-row-count tables rapidly, the session executes COPY INTO @~/export_stage/ FROM PROD_DB.PUBLIC.CUSTOMER_RECORDS FILE_FORMAT=(TYPE=CSV COMPRESSION=GZIP) followed by GET @~/export_stage/ file:///tmp/, logging large BYTES_WRITTEN_TO_RESULT and DATA_TRANSFER_HISTORY anomalies (logged in CloudTrail Event 1003 with QueryType=UNLOAD , COPY INTO @~ User Stage followed by GET_FILES, RowsUnloaded=4,820,190 rows , ~1.94 GB scanned, IncidentResponseAction=ALTER USER SVC_BI_ANALYTICS SET DISABLED = TRUE; SELECT SYSTEM$ABORT_SESSION, 884120994102; so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes SELECT QUERY_ID, USER_NAME, QUERY_TEXT, ROWS_UNLOADED, BYTES_WRITTEN_TO_RESULT FROM SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.QUERY_HISTORY WHERE QUERY_TYPE IN ('UNLOAD', 'GET_FILES') AND START_TIME >= DATEADD(day, -7, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP); (which executes a structured SQL query or database administration command , SELECT QUERY_ID, USER_NAME, QUERY_TEXT, ROWS_UNLOADED, BYTES_WRITTEN_TO_RESULT so that pivots from database query access or SQL injection to direct operating system command execution or authentication bypass , T1530 during "Bulk Table Staging via COPY INTO @~ & GET File Egress Forensics" under the database daemon's service account). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ COPY INTO @~/staging_dump/customers.csv.gz FROM PROD_DB.PUBLIC.CUSTOMER_RECORDS FILE_FORMAT=(TYPE=CSV COMPRESSION=GZIP); / ⇠#3 ACK 1003) from Node ③ (#3 Snowflake Network Policy Gate) to Node ④ (#4 Snowflake Virtual Warehouse), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Customer PII Tables & Internal Stage).
